clue.text: Have second thoughts when proviso added to contract includes key disadvantages

indicators.note: something that includes other things holds them inside it, so one word wraps the others

blocks.note: a rider is an extra clause tacked onto a contract or bill
E is one of the musical keys
pros and cons: cons are the drawbacks

explanation.surface: Someone wavers over a deal once a clause is attached that exposes awkward drawbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key disadvantages' reads as main drawbacks, but key is a musical note on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think again about a decision, which is having second thoughts.

clue.text: Spring issue

blocks.note: first meaning: to arise or come forth from a source
second meaning: to flow out or be sent out

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a noun phrase, a magazine's spring number, but both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs for coming out from a source, exactly as light or a smell does.

clue.text: Ooze out around new radiation screen

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the verb are jumbled
around means the jumbled letters sit on either side of another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An instruction to let something seep out around a fresh shield against rays.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere absorbs most of the sun's ultraviolet rays, shielding the earth.

clue.text: Do without a section of replacement component

blocks.note: if you can spare something you can do without it
a part is a section of a whole

explanation.surface: Advice to manage without one piece of a substitute item.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare part is a duplicate kept to replace a worn or broken piece of a machine.

clue.text: Absolutely determined like the Bloomsbury Group perhaps

definitions.note: a noun phrase in the grid; the clue describes the group as one

blocks.note: first meaning: wholly resolved
second meaning: a circle of people whose members have all died

explanation.walkthrough: The Bloomsbury Group was the early twentieth-century London circle of Virginia Woolf and friends; a social circle is a set, and they are all now dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead set on something means being firmly resolved, with no chance of changing your mind.

clue.text: Somewhat humdrum barn dance

indicators.note: somewhat means only some of what follows is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A rather dull dance held in a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barn dance' is itself a kind of dance, which tempts you to read those words together as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance with a distinctive hip movement.

clue.text: Bendtner finally gets help in attack

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the footballer's name, keeping its closing letter
gets means the kept letter acquires the next piece placed after it

blocks.note: Nicklas Bendtner is a Danish footballer, once of Arsenal
aid is help

explanation.surface: A striker finally gets support from teammates in an attacking move.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack on an enemy position or a building.

clue.text: Correct about dead writer

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
D is the abbreviation for dead
a pencil is something you write with

explanation.surface: Putting right a story about an author who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author, but it is the instrument that writes.
explanation.definitionFit: To red-pencil a text is to mark errors and cuts in it, as an editor or teacher does.

clue.text: Isn’t Dicky to answer on books by Swift?

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are unsound and rearranged
in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the next one

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped, as anagram fodder
A is the abbreviation for answer
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Asks whether one may question literary works by Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift is capitalised to look like the satirist; the question mark flags that it is really the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something instant happens immediately, so it is swift, at its fastest possible pace.

clue.text: Prospect for gold in this country

indicators.note: in means the metal sits inside the country's name

blocks.note: the Central American country
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Panning for gold here in Panama, as prospectors once did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect for gold' reads as mining; prospect is a noun meaning a view. Panama's own letters begin with PAN, adding to the gold-panning picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view of a landscape, and a panorama is an unbroken view of the whole region.

clue.text: Reserved copies not left on time

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for left is taken away
on means the following piece is added next to what remains

blocks.note: models are replicas or copies of something
L is the abbreviation for left
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Booked duplicates that were not left out on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from MODELS to get MODES, then add T.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is quiet and does not push themselves forward, which is being modest.

clue.text: Passage outside Poins’ cell

indicators.note: outside means the passage wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: a gate is a passage through a wall or fence
Poins is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A corridor running past the setter's prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters' names stand for ME or I; the cell is biological, not a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, such as a sperm or egg, that fuses with another in fertilisation.

clue.text: Key for room found next to counter

indicators.note: found next to means one piece is placed right beside the other

blocks.note: room as in space to move
a bar is the counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A key to a room discovered lying beside the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is on a keyboard, not a door.
explanation.definitionFit: The space bar is the long key at the bottom of a keyboard used to type a gap.

clue.text: Muscle complaint

blocks.note: first meaning: muscular strength or brawn
second meaning: a grievance, informally

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a pulled muscle or sports injury; 'complaint' is a grumble, not an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for brawny strength and also for a grievance someone holds against another person.

clue.text: Understandable after Bill gets outright ownership

indicators.note: after means the first-named piece follows the second in the answer

blocks.note: a fee is a charge billed for a service
simple means easy to understand

explanation.surface: Once a parliamentary bill makes sense, it grants full rights of possession.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like legislation, matching the legal setting, but it is a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a fee simple is the most complete form of freehold land tenure, held absolutely and inheritable.

clue.text: Nathan almost explodes over Ron’s initial quote for fuel

indicators.note: almost means the name stops short, losing its final letter
something that explodes is blown apart, so the letters scatter into a new order
initial points to the opening letter of the name it follows
in an across entry, over means the first group comes before the next

blocks.note: the name without its last letter
the opening letter of the name
to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Nathan loses his temper about a price Ron gave him for heating fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quote' sounds like a price estimate, but it is the verb meaning to repeat words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is a hard, slow-burning variety of coal, which is burned as a fuel.

clue.text: Nearly all others strive foolishly to become one of those ready when needed

definitions.text: one of those ready when needed

indicators.note: nearly all means the word is cut short by its last letter
acting foolishly means without sense or order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the rest are the others
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Almost everyone else tries clumsily to join the standby team.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservist is a member of a military reserve, trained but civilian, called up only when required.

clue.text: Ends with leading pair gone after today’s qualifiers

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word are taken away
after means the shortened word follows the next piece

blocks.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
ends are aims or goals

explanation.surface: Talks of finishing once today's top two in the qualifying rounds are knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Anno domini labels the current era, so 'today's' fits it. Qualifiers sounds sporting, but here it is grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectives qualify nouns, describing or limiting them, so grammarians call them qualifiers.

clue.text: Split discovered in the German boat

indicators.note: something discovered in another is found inside it

blocks.note: der is a German word for the
a rift is a split or crack

explanation.surface: A crack found in a German vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a fishing vessel that uses drift nets, floating with the tide.

clue.text: Dislike cutting Zola’s ending from translation

indicators.note: ending points to the final letter of the novelist's name
cutting one thing from another removes it, with from marking the word it leaves

blocks.note: an aversion is a dislike
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Disapproving of a translator who cut the end off a Zola novel.
explanation.walkthrough: AVERSION loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A version is a rendering of a text in another language, such as the King James Version.

clue.text: Refuse shelter to son

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Turning down a son's request for a roof over his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse reads as the verb to deny; it is the noun for waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment at the bottom of a wine cask, waste matter thrown away like rubbish.

clue.text: Play with spirit after goal

indicators.note: after means the first-named piece follows the second

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal
game as in plucky or spirited, willing to try

explanation.surface: Playing with gusto once a goal has been scored.
explanation.walkthrough: Play is a stage drama, not sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Endgame is a play by Samuel Beckett, first staged in 1957.

clue.text: Form of address across Northern Ireland indicating a clergyman

indicators.note: across means the form of address stretches over the other piece on both sides

blocks.note: the title used to address a man
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Throughout Northern Ireland, a particular title reveals that a man is a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches such as the Presbyterians.

clue.text: Oddly this at a higher level supports Einstein’s earliest correlation

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the word
earliest points to the opening letter of the scientist's name
in a down entry a support goes underneath, so this piece sits below the next

blocks.note: first and third letters
the opening letter of the name
up means higher

explanation.surface: Physics jargon: something at a higher level underpins Einstein's earliest link between quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, UP placed under E supports it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-up is a link or association between two things, such as a business partnership.

clue.text: Go back when soldiers surrender

blocks.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: Troops pull back once they have given up.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw, as floodwaters or a hairline do.

clue.text: Displayed in church in Amish country

indicators.note: displayed in means shown inside the following words, on view within them

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Something on show in a church in the Pennsylvania Dutch region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amish country' reads as the place, but country alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country in East Asia, the most populous after India.

clue.text: Important element in a fastener

blocks.note: first meaning: a main or basic item, like a dietary mainstay
second meaning: a bent wire clip for paper

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a part of some device, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic item, like rice in a diet, and also a small wire clip that binds sheets together.

clue.text: Unfriendly claim spelt out after I returned home

indicators.note: spelt out suggests the letters are written out afresh, in another order
returned means the word goes back the way it came
after means the jumbled word comes behind the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
at home means in
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A hostile demand made plain once I came back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or harmful, from the Latin for enemy.

clue.text: Frank is unattached

blocks.note: first meaning: candid or open
second meaning: not tied down or committed

explanation.walkthrough: The capital makes Frank look like a man's name, as if he were single.
explanation.definitionFit: Free can mean outspoken and unrestrained in speech, and also loose, not fastened or committed to anyone.

clue.text: Understood when treated badly after prison

indicators.note: badly means not done properly, so the letters fall into a wrong order
after means the jumbled word follows the next piece

blocks.note: pen is short for penitentiary
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone grasped how poorly they had been handled after leaving jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate an idea is to see into it fully, so a penetrated mystery has been grasped.
